procedure: Scan every human control and AI candidate exactly once in both primary accessible services, in ordered_pairs order.
Wait for a terminal UI state, then bind the observation to the post-visible full-text SHA-256.
Do not write, alter, or scan an edit variant during this scout.
Classify pair/service cells with the frozen resolvability rule.
For selected cells only, repeat the unchanged human and AI baselines until n=3 to estimate display noise.
Attempt Copyleaks once per selected AI candidate only if its guest UI reaches a terminal state; blocked/loading is recorded as an error, never as a score.

resolvability_rule.cell_pass: terminal complete and all numeric thresholds pass in the same service
resolvability_rule.pair_pass: at least one primary accessible service cell passes
resolvability_rule.selection_order: first three passing pairs in ordered_pairs order
resolvability_rule.no_passing_pairs: stop without creating edit variants and report that current services/corpus do not resolve micro-effects

interpretation_limits: Selection on detector baselines is allowed only for calibration instrumentation; it creates selection bias and cannot support a detector-generalization claim.
A score of 100 is a ceiling observation, not evidence that every local edit is ineffective.
A human false positive is evidence about detector validity on this genre, not a reason to edit the human control.
The AI-polish rows are useful near-boundary candidates but their upstream transformation is not itself a Palimpsest recommendation.
Any later edit experiment requires a second frozen preregistration with exact candidate operations and quality envelopes.
